title: Tableau Desktop Commands Reference (User-Invoked)
description: Commands used or referenced in Tableau Desktop that are invoked by user action. For third-party agents (e.g. MCP) targeting authoring-enabled Tableau Desktop.

generation.input_summary: Generated from command usage analysis, codegen command metadata, code-derived descriptions, workbook-state analysis, user-initiated overrides, and affordance mappings.

legacy_command_summary.note: Legacy commands (codegen.source == 'legacy') with args recovered from C++ Validate methods. See agent_guidance.legacy_commands_note.

defaults.how_invoked: Menu, toolbar, context menu, or keyboard shortcut.

agent_guidance.usage_notes: Invoke via ExecuteCommand(CommandId, params). Use serialized.name when calling from JavaScript. agent.can_invoke assumes an authoring-enabled Tableau Desktop runtime that injects context-filled params (e.g. UPI_Workspace) at execution time; callers should not serialize or pass those params. Only required binary/unserialized params outside that runtime-filled set block agent.can_invoke. Commands with agent.opens_blocking_dialog: true open a blocking UI dialog and can cause CDP socket hang. Evidence paths and usage_count may include references from test/ and testlib/; treat those as non-customer usage.
agent_guidance.recommendation_when_no_invocable_match: No authoring-enabled Desktop agent-invocable command found for this action. Use workbook JSON editing instead.
agent_guidance.context_filled_param_types_note: Authoring-enabled Tableau Desktop provides these at runtime; they do not set agent.requires_binary_or_unserialized_args and do not block agent.can_invoke.
agent_guidance.non_mcp_friendly_param_types_note: Parameters with type_id in this set cannot be supplied directly by an MCP caller (unserialized/pointers/UI handles). Context-filled parameters in this set are supplied by the authoring-enabled Desktop runtime.
agent_guidance.parameter_type_enums_note: For enum-backed parameters (type_id key), use the listed 'values' when constructing command arguments; 'serialized' is what to send (e.g. via MCP).
agent_guidance.parameter_type_formats_note: For OPAQUE non-enum params (serialized IDs, UUIDs, sheet/field locators, qualified names, pres-model objects, geometry), reference_data.parameter_type_formats (keyed by type_id) gives the exact wire format, a concrete example, whether an agent can construct the value (agent_constructable: yes/conditional/no), and how to obtain a valid one. Each matching command parameter also carries a compact invocation.parameters[].value_format hint pointing (detail_ref) at the full record. Grounded in monolith C++ serializers/param declarations/tests.
agent_guidance.modifies_workbook_state_note: Whether the command changes workbook/document content or persistent state (sheets, data, formatting, zones). true = modifies; false = does not (e.g. navigation, menus, dialogs, read-only); depends = effect depends on context (e.g. Undo/Redo, conditional mutation paths). Determined by C++ code analysis of each command's ::Do() implementation, then applied inline to invocation.modifies_workbook_state.
agent_guidance.command_relevant_to_environments_note: Environments where the command is relevant. Slugs: desktop (Tableau Desktop), web-server (web authoring on Tableau Server), web-cloud (web authoring on Tableau Cloud). Derived from codegen project (Doc/UI) and server_permission (WEB_AUTHORING adds web-server and web-cloud).
agent_guidance.legacy_commands_note: Commands with codegen.source == 'legacy' are declared via `legacy_command` in codegen and carry no codegen-declared parameters. Their arguments are recovered from the C++ <Name>Command::Validate method (codegen.args_source == 'cpp_validate', or 'cpp_validate_base' when inherited from an Abstract<Name> base), or, when no Validate exists, a heuristic scan of the handler body (args_source == 'cpp_do_scan'). args_source == 'none' means arguments could not be determined (the command is likely parameterless / context-only, but this is unconfirmed). codegen.source_file points at the C++ implementation. editor_type and server_permission are unknown for legacy commands.
agent_guidance.complex_args_note: agent.requires_complex_args flags commands with at least one REQUIRED input argument that an external/agent caller is unlikely to be able to construct without help from the live application (presentation models, runtime IDs/handles, geometry/positions, or vectors of identifiers). Unlike agent.requires_binary_or_unserialized_args, this does NOT block agent.can_invoke — the value is serializable in principle but needs structured or runtime knowledge. agent.complex_args lists each such input parameter with its category. A future construction helper should target these. First-pass classification; see complex_arg_categories for category meanings.

complex_arg_categories.presentation_model_or_config: Structured presentation-model or configuration object; must be built from live document state, not a simple literal.
complex_arg_categories.runtime_identifier_or_handle: Runtime-assigned identifier or opaque handle; not knowable without querying the live application.
complex_arg_categories.geometry_or_position: Coordinate/position in viz or canvas space; depends on the live layout.
complex_arg_categories.vector_of_names: Vector of names / qualified names; requires knowing exact catalog, field, or resource identifiers.

value_format.how_to_obtain: Query the live object graph, do not invent. Call tabdocobjectgraph GetObjectGraph / BuildObjectGraphPresModel (DPI_ObjectGraph pres-model, codegen/doc/pres-models/objectgraph.data). Each node in the DPI_ObjectGraphNodes array carries ObjectId (wire key data-object-model-object-id) alongside Caption (object-caption). Read the id off the node whose caption matches the object you want. GetActiveObjectId returns the currently active object's id. For trivial single-table sources the id often equals the table caption, but this is not guaranteed for relation/extract-derived nodes.

The 'refline'+index format is trivially predictable, but the index is only meaningful relative to reference lines that already exist in the target worksheet's default pane. To target an existing line, read the real id from the reference-line pres model (ReferenceLineBuilder::SetId(spec.GetId()) at ReferenceLineBuilder.cpp:117). For CREATING a new line the id is generated server-side via GenerateID()/NextIDNumber(0), so the caller does not supply it.

BUT it is populated at runtime by BuildVisualIDPresModel(IWorkbookAccessor, VisualID), which validates the sheet exists in the workbook (throws LogicException if not) and resolves story path (storyboard/story-point-id). Real values are surfaced in pres models such as GetSheetsInfo/workbook (DPI_VisualIDPMs 'visual-ids' collection) and explain-data-pane. Prefer reading it from a pres-model query rather than hand-building.

Use the exact dashboard display name (dashboards ARE base sheets in the workbook's sheet list). Query via GetSheetsInfo, or read <dashboard name='...'> in the TWB.

DPI_AddInLocator.format: AddInLocatorPresModel struct (JSON object). Fields (from codegen/doc/pres-models/extensions.data:13-18): add-in-instance-id (string, required), add-in-type (enum: 'invalid'|'dashboard'|'worksheet'|'workspace'), sheet-path (SheetPathPresModel, present only for dashboard extensions, else null), visual-id-pres-model (VisualIDPresModel array, present only for worksheet extensions, else null). The add-in-instance-id is a runtime UNDECORATED-HEX TUUID (32 hex chars, no braces/dashes - TUUIDFormatOption::Hex), derived from the extension zone's SimpleIdentifier at creation via ExtensionDocFactory::GetInstanceIdFromSimpleIdentifier.
DPI_AddInLocator.example_source: modules/platform/tabextensionregistration/main/extension/ExtensionDocFactory.cpp:11-15 (TUUID idAsTUUID(id.ToString()); return idAsTUUID.ToString(TUUIDFormatOption::Hex);) - example uuid value is illustrative; obtain the real hex from a zone/extension query
DPI_AddInLocator.how_to_obtain: The add-in-instance-id is a runtime handle minted when the extension zone is created; the caller cannot invent it. Obtain the full locator from a pres-model that emits it: ExtensionZoneInfoProvider (dashboard: BuildDashboardLocator(zone->GetExtensionDoc()->GetInstanceId(), sheetPath)), MarksCardPresModelBuilder (worksheet: BuildWorksheetLocator(...)), or any AddInLocator-carrying event (reloadAddIn/blockExtension/ContextMenuEvent/etc.). Reuse the whole object returned; do not hand-build it.
DPI_AddInLocator.gotchas: instance-id uses TUUIDFormatOption::Hex (undecorated 32-char hex) - this DIFFERS from window-id which uses DecoratedHex with braces. sheet-path vs visual-id-pres-model are mutually exclusive by extension type (dashboard vs worksheet); workspace locators carry only the instance id. Runtime-scoped; not stable across sessions.

DPI_Calculation.format: CalculationPresModel struct (JSON object), defined in codegen/doc/pres-models/calculation.data:13-53. It is a rich config object, NOT just a formula string - but the load-bearing content is Formula (wire key calculation-formula). Other fields (all defaulted): datasource, calculation-caption, field-name, folder-name/role, scope-isolation, has-table-calc-data, type-in-pill fields, calc-editor-text-selection, functions pres model, calculation-context, error info, style tokens, etc. In practice it is emitted as a command RESULT/output (read via result->Get<ConstCalculationPresModelPtr>(DPI_Calculation) then GetFormula()), not typically supplied by an external caller.
DPI_Calculation.how_to_obtain: Primarily an output: run a calculation command and read the CalculationPresModel from the response; its Formula field is the meaningful payload. As an input it requires a full pres-model with many interdependent fields (type-in-pill fields gated on GetIsTypeInPill(), functions PM non-null, etc.), so an agent should not hand-build it; drive calc edits through formula-string params (e.g. calculation-formula / the calc dialog commands) instead.
DPI_Calculation.gotchas: Do not confuse the object with a bare formula string - the formula lives in the child field calculation-formula. DPI_TypeInPill uses the same struct. Formulas are stored in name-form (ConvertFormulaToNames) internally. Read paths (GetFormula) are stable; write paths expect the app-built pres model.

DPI_ChildObjectId.format: Opaque object-graph node id of the RIGHT endpoint / child object in the relationship editor. Same encoding as DPI_DataObjectModelObjectId: plain TString (DataObjectModel::ObjectId), NOT a UUID and NOT a QualifiedName. Declared as [TString, string, simple] (codegen/doc/params.data:2269). Set via params->Set<TString>(DPI_ChildObjectId, childId.GetValue()).
DPI_ChildObjectId.example_source: modules/platform/tabdocobjectgraph/main/commands/ObjectModelCommands.cpp:308 (params->Set<TString>(DPI_ChildObjectId, childId.GetValue())); ObjectModelCommands.cpp:256-262 pairs DPI_ParentObjectId/DPI_ChildObjectId with eligibleId.GetValue()/objectId.GetValue(); objectgraph-cmd.data:91,110,116 declare it required alongside ParentObjectId
DPI_ChildObjectId.how_to_obtain: Same as DPI_ParentObjectId: read node ids from the GetObjectGraph pres-model (DPI_ObjectGraphNodes -> data-object-model-object-id). Child is the right/many side of the relationship.
DPI_ChildObjectId.gotchas: Always paired with DPI_ParentObjectId for relationship-editor commands. Not a UUID; not a QualifiedName. Empty string is NO_OBJECT_ID.

DPI_ControllerId.format: Unsigned 32-bit integer (uint32_t on the wire - declared under the 'type: [ uint32_t, uint, simple ]' header, NOT a string). It is a ControllerID = ComponentID = uint32_t runtime handle into the per-workbook ComponentManager (the 'PersistantDataController'). Values are handed out sequentially starting at 1 (ComponentID_First); 0 = ComponentID_Invalid. Wraps at uint32 max; reused after Release.
DPI_ControllerId.example_source: modules/platform/tabcore/main/interface/ComponentManager.cpp:7 (m_nextComponentID(ComponentID_First)); ComponentManager.h:25-45 (Add<T>() assigns then post-increments); HierarchySelectCommands.cpp:46-59 round-trip
DPI_ControllerId.how_to_obtain: Runtime handle valid only as a live entry in that session's ComponentManager. Cannot be fabricated. First invoke the 'create controller' command (e.g. CreateHierarchySelectController), read the emitted controller-id from the response (SetControllerId / the destroy-command params), then feed that exact value back into follow-up commands. Guessing '1' may collide with or point at an unrelated component.
DPI_ControllerId.gotchas: Per-ComponentManager (per workbook controller), ephemeral, reused after Release, wraps at uint32 max. 0 = invalid sentinel.

DPI_Dashboard.format: The dashboard's exact DISPLAY NAME as a plain string. Parameters::SetDashboard -> Set<TString>(DPI_Dashboard, locator.Sheetname()); built back into a SheetLocator from the name on read. A story-point (ephemeral) dashboard instead serializes a SheetPath object under the sibling key 'dashboard-pm' (DPI_DashboardPM, 'corresponds to DPI_Dashboard'); persistent dashboards always use the plain name string.
DPI_Dashboard.example_source: modules/integration_tests/current/filtercommands_integ/test/FilterCommandsCategoricalTest.cpp:330 (params->Set(DPI_Dashboard, TString(u"Dashboard 1"))); also u"dash-with-qf" at :522 and real UI producer modules/desktop/tabui/main/dashboard/qtdesktop/ZoneOverlayWidget.cpp:1302 sets it to dashboard.GetLocator()
DPI_Dashboard.how_to_obtain: Use the exact dashboard display name (dashboards ARE base sheets in the workbook's sheet list). Query via GetSheetsInfo, or read <dashboard name='...'> in the TWB.
DPI_Dashboard.gotchas: ValidateParameters::ValidateDashboard resolves the name and checks it is a real dashboard; a nonexistent name or a worksheet/storyboard name -> BadValue. Not a UUID. Empty when required -> BadValue; 'implicit' so absent falls back to the current dashboard context.

DPI_DashboardObjectHandle.format: C++ type `ObjectIdentifier`, which is a subclass of `SimpleIdentifier` (formalism/ObjectIdentifier.h). Serialized via `ObjectIdentifierSerializer` whose `TypeToString` returns `id.ToString()` and `TypeFromString` calls `ObjectIdentifier(str)`. Because it inherits SimpleIdentifier, ToString() is a TUUID DecoratedHex braced UUID: `{XXXXXXXX-XXXX-XXXX-XXXX-XXXXXXXXXXXX}` (same wire form as DPI_WindowID). params.data lists its category as `object` but the actual on-wire value is that UUID string, not a JSON struct.
DPI_DashboardObjectHandle.example: {runtime-braced-UUID, e.g. {D4FD3F72-3E18-46F1-A978-7405AF5031FE}} - no literal appears in tests; ButtonTests asserts equality against buttonZonePresModel->GetZoneCommon()->GetExtendedObjectHandle().ToString(), confirming it is an ObjectIdentifier round-tripped through ToString()
DPI_DashboardObjectHandle.how_to_obtain: Purely a runtime handle: created via `ObjectIdentifier::Create()` and attached to extended-object zones (buttons, images, etc.) at runtime; read back through `Zone::GetExtendedObjectHandle()`. To get a live value, query `tabdoc:get-dashboard` -> DashboardPresModel -> ZoneCommon.ExtendedObjectHandle (property mapped to DPI_DashboardObjectHandle). Only present when the zone has an extended object (non-null); ordinary viz/text zones have a null handle.
DPI_DashboardObjectHandle.gotchas: Not agent-inventable - an invented or stale UUID resolves to no object (BadValue). Handle is non-null only for extended-object zones; command wrappers guard with `!val.IsNull()`. Distinct from DPI_ObjectIdentifier / DPI_DashboardObjectNewObjectHandle which share the same ObjectIdentifier type. The value is a session-runtime id, not persisted stably in the TWB.

DPI_DataObjectModelObjectId.format: Opaque application-assigned object-graph node id. NOT a UUID and NOT the ObjectIdentifierSerializer/SimpleIdentifier braced-UUID form. Declared in codegen as plain [TString, string, simple] (codegen/doc/params.data type block starting line 1430). At runtime the value is a DataObjectModel::ObjectId, which is just a thin wrapper over a TString (ObjectId::GetValue()). Commands read/write it via params->Set<TString>(DPI_DataObjectModelObjectId, objectId.GetValue()). The string is whatever key the object-graph controller assigned to a node: for a single logical table it is typically the table caption/name (e.g. "Actors", "Movies", "Y"); for relation-derived objects it is a relation key such as "FK_DimProductCategory_9EF755CF2AA74E508A169E1D94E05572" or "Extract (Extract.Extract)_11D82FE28E5A4E62BDA6CD55488F4563". Treat as an opaque handle.
DPI_DataObjectModelObjectId.example_source: modules/integration_tests/current/tabdocobjectgraph_integ/test/ObjectModelCommandIntegTest.cpp:151-156 (ACTORS_OBJECT_ID=u"Actors", APPEARANCES_OBJECT_ID=u"Appearances"), :3454 (params->Set<TString>(DPI_DataObjectModelObjectId, u"Y")); relation-key form at :107-134 (CATEGORY_OBJECT_ID=u"FK_DimProductCategory_9EF755CF2AA74E508A169E1D94E05572"); DataObjectGraphCommandTest.cpp:674 (SetObjectId(u"Actors"))
DPI_DataObjectModelObjectId.how_to_obtain: Query the live object graph, do not invent. Call tabdocobjectgraph GetObjectGraph / BuildObjectGraphPresModel (DPI_ObjectGraph pres-model, codegen/doc/pres-models/objectgraph.data). Each node in the DPI_ObjectGraphNodes array carries ObjectId (wire key data-object-model-object-id) alongside Caption (object-caption). Read the id off the node whose caption matches the object you want. GetActiveObjectId returns the currently active object's id. For trivial single-table sources the id often equals the table caption, but this is not guaranteed for relation/extract-derived nodes.
DPI_DataObjectModelObjectId.gotchas: Do NOT assume a UUID: a separate DPI_ObjectIdentifier/DPI_DashboardObjectIdentifier param uses ObjectIdentifierSerializer (SimpleIdentifier -> TUUID DecoratedHex braced UUID), but these object-graph id params do not. Passing a UUID or a bracketed QualifiedName where the graph expects a caption-style key will fail to resolve. Note the sibling param DPI_ObjectIdQualifiedName (object-id-qualified-name) is an ALTERNATE representation of an object id in QualifiedName format for some flows; the plain object-id params here are the opaque-string form. Empty string ("") is the well-known NO_OBJECT_ID sentinel.

DPI_ElementInstanceId.format: Polymorphic StyleContext ID token whose exact string depends on the formattable element type. Three observed forms: (1) reference line -> 'refline<N>' (same string as reference-line-id, N a non-negative int index); (2) annotation -> 'annotation_<k>' (story-delta: 'addedDelta_annotation_<k>'), k an int; (3) legend -> a fixed closed-set token: 'legend-color' | 'legend-shape' | 'legend-size' | 'legend-highlight' | 'legend-map'. NOT a UUID. Empty string is valid and means 'the whole sheet / all lines' rather than one instance.
DPI_ElementInstanceId.example_source: modules/integration_tests/current/formatting_integ/main/SetSheetStyleReferenceLineFormattingTests.cpp:50 (m_reflineId = u"refline1"; then .SetElementInstanceId(m_reflineId) at :418); legend tokens in tabstylemodel/main/style/StyleContext.cpp:291-310
DPI_ElementInstanceId.how_to_obtain: Legends: constructable from the fixed closed set (legend-color/shape/size/highlight/map). Reflines/annotations: NOT blindly constructable - the index only resolves against elements already existing in the target worksheet's default pane; obtain the real value from the reference-line pres model (ReferenceLineBuilder SetId) or annotation spec, or from the style-contexts array emitted by set-sheet-style-* commands.
DPI_ElementInstanceId.gotchas: For a reference line, element-instance-id IS the reference-line-id (refline<N>); element-instance-id is the broader/polymorphic wrapper also covering annotations and legends. Refline/annotation indices are reused after deletion (first free slot), so not a stable permanent identity across edits - do not cache across mutations. Empty string means whole-sheet, not an error.

DPI_ExtensionContextMenuId.format: Plain TString. An author-supplied id declared in the extension's .trex manifest context-menu-items (menuItem.id), NOT system-generated. In this monolith snapshot the manifest parser only recognizes the reserved <configure-context-menu-item/> tag and hard-codes id = 'configure', so the only currently valid value is 'configure'. The id is emitted per registered item in the ContextMenuEvent pres-model when a menu item is clicked.
DPI_ExtensionContextMenuId.how_to_obtain: Known author-chosen string from the manifest, not random. Discoverable via ExtensionRegistration::GetContextMenuItemIds(). An agent can predict/reuse it (currently only 'configure'), but the platform validates ids against the manifest (VerifyContextMenuIdsInput throws on unknown/duplicate), so an arbitrary invented id is rejected. Only meaningful if the extension's manifest declares the item AND a matching callback is registered at initializeAsync.
DPI_ExtensionContextMenuId.gotchas: The ids passed to initializeAsync (DPI_ExtensionContextMenuIds, wire key extension-context-menu-ids, a list) must exactly match manifest-registered ids with no duplicates or the command throws. JS SDK looks up contextMenuFunctions[event.id] and throws 'Received unexpected context menu Id from event' if the id was not registered by the author.

DPI_FieldName.format: A Tableau structured field UNIQUE-NAME (QualifiedName), NOT the user-facing caption. Bracketed, dot-separated components: [<datasource>].[<column-instance>]. The leaf column-instance is itself Tableau's encoded form <agg>:<column>:<type-code> (e.g. none:Category:nk for an unaggregated dimension, sum:Budget Payroll:qk for a SUM measure). A closing bracket inside a component is escaped by doubling it (]]). Serialized C++-side by FieldNameSerializer::TypeToString -> FieldName::GetFullValue() (returns the full bracketed string); parsed inbound by FieldName::ParseGlobal(str). Local (single-component) form like [Product] is also accepted. Empty string is rejected (BadValue).
DPI_FieldName.example_source: modules/tools/tqv/testpass/fixtures/superstore-abstractquery.aq:3 (column='[Sample - Superstore].[none:Category:nk]'); measure form [Starbucks (mssql)].[sum:Budget Payroll:qk] in VisualPresModelBuilderTest.cpp:807 via _fn literal (=ParseGlobal)
DPI_FieldName.how_to_obtain: Must reference a field that actually exists in the live workbook's global namespace. When the param is required, ValidateParameters::ValidateField calls m_workbookAccessor->GetConstNamespace().HasField(fn) and emits BadValue if the field is unknown. Obtain the exact unique-name from the running app (schema viewer / field-list query / GetFields-style PM), or read column='...' / <field>[...]</field> strings from the TWB/TWBX <datasource>. Do NOT hand-type the caption ('Category'); the wire wants the encoded unique-name ([ds].[none:Category:nk]).
DPI_FieldName.gotchas: 1) Caption != unique-name: 'Category' (display) is wrong; the wire form is [ds].[none:Category:nk]. 2) The <agg>:<col>:<typecode> leaf (none/sum/... : name : nk/qk/ok) is a column-instance encoding produced once a field is used; a bare dimension may also appear as [ds].[Field] or local [Field]. 3) 'automatic validation' is implied by this DPI id — an unknown or empty field name becomes BadValue (surfaces as an opaque Agent 500). Use a non-validating id (see doc/params.data, e.g. DPI_FilterFieldName / DPI_FieldNameLocal) if you must pass an unresolved name. 4) Wire key is the terse 'fn', not 'field-name' (that key belongs to DPI_FieldNameString).
source_files: codegen/data/params.data:526,533 (type FieldName string simple; [DPI_FieldName, fn, "FieldName with automatic validation"])

DPI_FieldNameString.format: A PLAIN raw string (TString), NOT a FieldName-typed param. Declared under type [TString, string, simple] (params.data line ~1430 block), so it passes through TStringSerializer verbatim with NO ParseGlobal and NO namespace validation. Its documented purpose is still 'The global field name', so callers put the SAME textual unique-name ([<datasource>].[<column-instance>]) into it, but the wire treats it as an opaque string.

DPI_FieldNameString.how_to_obtain: As a raw string it is trivially constructable, but to be meaningful it should still carry a real field's global unique-name (same source as DPI_FieldName: live field query or TWB datasource). No automatic validation happens on this param, so a wrong string will not be caught here — it will fail (or silently mis-target) downstream in the command that consumes it.
DPI_FieldNameString.gotchas: 1) Despite the wire key 'field-name' and description 'global field name', this is NOT the validated FieldName type — it is a bare string. The validated field params are DPI_FieldName (key 'fn') and DPI_GlobalFieldName (key 'global-field-name'). 2) Because there is no ParseGlobal, malformed brackets are not rejected at parse time. 3) Do not confuse the wire key 'field-name' (this string param) with the FieldName-typed params.

DPI_FieldVector.format: A list of FieldName unique-name strings. Declared under type [FieldName, string, simplearray, , FieldName, ...]. Serialized via ParameterTypeSerializer<FieldName>::SerializeList -> DataSerializerHelpers::SerializeVector -> a ListStructure whose items are each FieldName::GetFullValue() (i.e. each element is the same [<datasource>].[<column-instance>] string as the scalar). On the JSON/Agent wire this is a JSON array of field-name strings (NOT a single delimited/joined string). Deserialized element-by-element with FieldName::ParseGlobal.
DPI_FieldVector.example_source: single-element real value: params->Set(DPI_FieldVector, FieldNameVec{TS("[Starbucks (mssql)].[sum:Budget Payroll:qk]"_fn)}) in modules/integration_tests/legacytest/main/presentation-model/visualization/VisualPresModelBuilderTest.cpp:807; multi-element strings from superstore-abstractquery.aq fixture; ListStructure(DPI_FieldVector, ss) in modules/feature-doc/docapi/main/serializers/ImageRegionInfoSerializer.cpp:30
DPI_FieldVector.how_to_obtain: Build a JSON array; each element is a real field unique-name obtained the same way as DPI_FieldName (live field/schema query or TWB datasource). Elements are the encoded unique-names, not captions.
DPI_FieldVector.gotchas: 1) It is an ARRAY of strings, not one comma/semicolon-joined string — serialized as a ListStructure (ss.ListItem per element). 2) Each element is the encoded unique-name ([ds].[none:Col:nk]); captions do not work. 3) The scalar variants of the same underlying type exist under different wire keys (e.g. DPI_FieldNames='field-names') so pick the key the specific command declares; DPI_FieldVector's key is 'field-vector'. 4) Whether elements are namespace-validated depends on the consuming command (DPI_FieldVector itself is not routed through ValidateParameters::ValidateField, unlike DPI_FieldName/DPI_GlobalFieldName).

DPI_GlobalFieldName.format: Same wire encoding as DPI_FieldName: a structured field unique-name string [<datasource>].[<column-instance>] serialized via FieldNameSerializer (GetFullValue) and parsed with FieldName::ParseGlobal. This is the doc/params.data twin of the core DPI_FieldName; it also carries automatic validation. Distinguished from DPI_FieldName only by wire key ('global-field-name') and the codegen tree it is declared in.

DPI_GlobalFieldName.gotchas: 1) The params.data comment states DPI_GlobalFieldName IMPLIES automatic validation (ValidateParameters::ValidateField) — pass an unresolved/empty name and it becomes BadValue. Use a non-validating id (DPI_FilterFieldName documented as not validating global-namespace existence, or DPI_FieldNameLocal) when the field is in a private/extract namespace. 2) Same caption-vs-unique-name trap as DPI_FieldName. 3) Wire key differs from the core id: 'global-field-name' here vs 'fn' for DPI_FieldName.

DPI_NotificationId.format: Plain TString. NOT an integer, NOT a UUID, NOT an enum constant. An opaque round-trip correlation token used by the Analytics Assistant side pane (and web/close-UI commands) to correlate an async notification/pres-model back to the target chat item that triggered it. In the common flow it is caller-supplied and echoed back unchanged. One specific server path (NotificationType_LaunchFromCalcDialog) ignores the inbound value and assigns a process-global stringified counter ('0','1','2',...). Empty string is the 'none' sentinel and is dropped.
DPI_NotificationId.how_to_obtain: In the normal flow it is entirely caller-chosen: pick any non-empty string. Its only contract is that the same string is echoed back in the side-pane pres-model (SetNotificationId) so the client can match the response to the issuing chat item. Server does not validate format.
DPI_NotificationId.gotchas: Empty string means 'no notification id' and is dropped (guarded by if (!notificationId.isEmpty())). The LaunchFromCalcDialog path ignores any inbound value and assigns its own stringified static counter, so don't rely on your id surviving that notification type. No cross-session stability and no server-side uniqueness guarantee - uniqueness/meaning is the client's responsibility.

DPI_PaneSpecificationId.format: MarksSpecificationId = int (signed). Identifies which pane / marks-specification a command targets. Sentinel values (from ShelfModelTypes.h): -1 = cActiveId (the active pane specification, the default), -2 = cAllId (the 'All' model / all panes), -3 = cVisualSpecId (shelves global to the VisualSpecification). Concrete per-pane ids are non-negative (0,1,2,...) and are runtime-assigned; obtained via PaneSpecification::GetId(). SetPaneSpecId only sets the param when id >= 0.
DPI_PaneSpecificationId.example_source: ShelfModelTypes.h (cActiveId=-1); non-negative examples 0/1/2 in modules/integration_tests/current/tabdoc_integ/test/datagraph/features/DynamicColorRangeTest.cpp (0=all-pane path, 1/2 = individual panes)
DPI_PaneSpecificationId.how_to_obtain: Trivially an integer. To target the active pane without knowing runtime ids, pass -1 (cActiveId) — this is the framework default. Specific non-negative pane ids are assigned at runtime per viz (PaneSpecification::GetId()); read them from a live pres-model rather than guessing. Tests confirm the param carries a plain int: params->Has<int>(DPI_PaneSpecificationId) / Set<MarksSpecificationId>(DPI_PaneSpecificationId, 0).
DPI_PaneSpecificationId.gotchas: Signed — negative values are meaningful sentinels, not errors (-1 active, -2 all, -3 visual-spec-global). A raw non-negative index is only valid for the current viz layout; it is not a stable/portable id.

DPI_ParentObjectId.format: Opaque object-graph node id of the LEFT endpoint / parent object in the relationship editor. Same encoding as DPI_DataObjectModelObjectId: a plain TString (DataObjectModel::ObjectId), NOT a UUID and NOT a QualifiedName. Declared as [TString, string, simple] (codegen/doc/params.data:2268). Set via params->Set<TString>(DPI_ParentObjectId, parentId.GetValue()).
DPI_ParentObjectId.how_to_obtain: Same source as DPI_DataObjectModelObjectId: obtain node ids from GetObjectGraph (DPI_ObjectGraph pres-model, DPI_ObjectGraphNodes each with data-object-model-object-id + object-caption). The parent is the left/one side of the relationship. Relationship endpoints are also surfaced via DPI_ObjectGraphRelationship / RelationshipNodes in the same pres-model.
DPI_ParentObjectId.gotchas: Pairs with DPI_ChildObjectId; AddOrEditRelationship / relationship-editor commands require both (objectgraph-cmd.data lines 90-91, 109-110, 115-116, 142-143). Do not confuse with the join-oriented DPI_ForeignObjectId/DPI_PrimaryObjectId pair (foreign-object-id/primary-object-id) used by other relationship commands. Not a UUID; not a bracketed QualifiedName.

DPI_Position.format: Plain signed integer index (int). 0-based position; -1 indicates the end (the declared sentinel, used as the default via GetOptional<int>(DPI_Position, -1)). Semantics are context-dependent per command: sheet/tab insertion index (NewUIWorksheetCommand), dashboard zone z-order position (MoveFreeFormZoneInZOrder), drill level, encoding slot, etc. Consumed via params->Get<int>(DPI_Position).
DPI_Position.example_source: modules/platform/tabdoc/main/drillpath/commands/DrillPathCommands.cpp:447 (int pos = params->GetOptional<int>(DPI_Position, -1);); modules/desktop/tabui/main/sheetui/commands/NewUICommands.cpp:102-108 (0-based tab insert position, falls back to GetSheetInsertPosition())
DPI_Position.how_to_obtain: Constructable directly: supply a 0-based integer index, or -1 to append at the end. When omitted, most commands fall back to a context-appropriate default (e.g. GetSheetInsertPosition() for new sheets). Choose the index relative to the target collection's current ordering.
DPI_Position.gotchas: Meaning varies by command (tab index vs zone z-order vs drill level vs encoding slot) - always check the specific command. -1 = end/append, not an error. It is a plain int, not the uint32 store/controller handles.

DPI_PublishedDatasourceId.format: Plain TString. It is the server repository ID (repository-URL ID) of a published datasource the workbook is already connected to - the same value used as DPI_RepositoryUrl. NOT a REST-API LUID (UUID) and NOT a local id. It is RepositoryLocation::GetID(), the legacy dash-numeric repository id.
DPI_PublishedDatasourceId.how_to_obtain: Server-assigned when a datasource is published; obtainable only by discovery from the workbook's existing published-datasource connection - node->GetDatasourceUrl() / RepositoryLocation::GetID() (ObjectModelCommands.cpp:2174,2227). Cannot be fabricated.
DPI_PublishedDatasourceId.gotchas: It is a dash-numeric repository id (e.g. 314-592-653), NOT a UUID/LUID - do not pass a REST-API datasource LUID. Only set into the connect params when non-empty (ObjectModelUtils.cpp:111).

DPI_ReferenceLineSpecificationId.format: Literal string 'refline<N>' where <N> is a non-negative integer index (e.g. refline0, refline1, refline2). NOT a UUID/GUID and NOT a human-meaningful name. It is a per-worksheet reusable slot index (freed indices get reused) with the fixed prefix 'refline'. Minted by MakeID(index) = TFormat(u"refline%1", index); parsed back via GetIndexFromId (strips 'refline' prefix, toInt).
DPI_ReferenceLineSpecificationId.how_to_obtain: The 'refline'+index format is trivially predictable, but the index is only meaningful relative to reference lines that already exist in the target worksheet's default pane. To target an existing line, read the real id from the reference-line pres model (ReferenceLineBuilder::SetId(spec.GetId()) at ReferenceLineBuilder.cpp:117). For CREATING a new line the id is generated server-side via GenerateID()/NextIDNumber(0), so the caller does not supply it.
DPI_ReferenceLineSpecificationId.gotchas: Indices are reused after deletion (NextIDNumber returns first free slot) so reflineN is not stable identity across edits. Paired reference lines (bands / line+confidence-interval) have separate ids linked via GetPairedId()/GetPairedDistrId(); primary of a pair has GetId()==GetPrimaryId().

DPI_SchemaViewerSelector.format: C++ SchemaViewerSelectorPtr (SchemaViewerSelector : Selector) — a runtime set<QualifiedName> of fields/drill-paths/tables/folders selected in the data-pane schema viewer. In params.data it lives in the explicit 'parameters that aren't yet serialized' section: type is declared 'unserialized'. There is NO serializer, so it CANNOT be represented on the wire at all. Flagged 'implicit'.
DPI_SchemaViewerSelector.example_source: codegen/doc/params.data:5195-5197 ('parameters that aren't yet serialized' block, type ... unserialized)
DPI_SchemaViewerSelector.how_to_obtain: Cannot be sent by an external caller. It is a live UI-selection object built by the schema-viewer interaction layer; there is no wire encoding to construct or capture.
DPI_SchemaViewerSelector.gotchas: Even more restricted than DPI_Selector: DPI_Selector has a stub/POC serializer, but SchemaViewerSelector is declared 'unserialized' outright. Any command that truly requires it is not agent-invocable via this param.

DPI_Selector.format: C++ ConstSelectorCollectionPtr (SelectorCollection). params.data comment: 'selectors are not useable from browser, so mark jstype as object'; flagged 'implicit'. CRITICAL: the wire serializer is effectively a NO-OP — SelectorCollectionSerializer::ToSerializer is an empty stub (body is just '// TODO'), so a live selection does NOT round-trip to the wire. ToObject is a documented 'proof of concept' that reconstructs ONLY a tuple selection from a nested DPI_Table (a schema with a TupleId column); anything else returns nullptr.
DPI_Selector.example: (no reliable wire literal — serializer emits nothing)
DPI_Selector.how_to_obtain: Not directly constructable on the wire. The only path that materializes a selector from params is a nested DPI_Table carrying a TupleId column (tuple selection), and even that is flagged proof-of-concept. For field/pill commands, the practical alternative is DPI_ShelfItemID: FieldCommands validate with OneRequired<uint32_t, ConstSelectorCollectionPtr>(DPI_ShelfItemID, DPI_Selector), and ConstructSelectionParamFromID builds the selection from a shelf-item-id at runtime.
DPI_Selector.gotchas: ToSerializer is a stub — do not expect a captured selector value to be re-sendable. Runtime-only selection object. Where a command declares both, pass shelf-item-id instead of selector.

DPI_Sheet.format: The exact DISPLAY NAME of any base sheet (worksheet, dashboard, OR storyboard) as a plain string. This is the general sheet locator: Parameters::GetSheet builds a SheetLocator from the string and resolves it against the workbook (BaseSheetDoc). Serialized command form is literally command sheet="<name>". Story-point sheets use the object variant 'sheet-pm' (DPI_SheetPM); persistent sheets use the plain name.
DPI_Sheet.example_source: modules/platform/tabdoc/test/serializers/CommandsSerializersTest.cpp:86 (inParams->Set<TString>(DPI_Sheet, u"sheet name")); serialized wire form proven in the expected fixture as command: "test:test-command sheet=\"sheet name\"" (expected.singleitem.txt)
DPI_Sheet.how_to_obtain: Exact display name of a worksheet/dashboard/storyboard from the workbook. Query via GetSheetsInfo (returns the sheet names), or read the TWB sheet titles. This is the same key the goto-sheet arcana recommends via navigate-to-sheet ({ "sheet": "Sheet 2" }).
DPI_Sheet.gotchas: ValidateParameters::ValidateSheet resolves the name and requires workbook HasBaseSheet; nonexistent/misspelled name -> BadValue. NOT a UUID (that is window-id/DPI_WindowID) and NOT a JSON object on the wire. Empty when required -> BadValue; 'implicit' so absent falls back to the current sheet (this is why goto-sheet with args:{} is a silent no-op).

DPI_SheetName.format: A plain sheet-name string (TString). Distinct DPI id from DPI_Sheet but validated through the same ValidateSheet path (switch case falls into ValidateSheet), so semantically it is also an exact sheet display name. Used where a command needs a named destination/target sheet rather than the general locator (e.g. SwitchToDocument, ChangeWorkbookUIMode's target sheet). No SimpleIdentifier/path partner is used with it in practice; always the bare name string.
DPI_SheetName.example_source: modules/platform/tabdoc/test/workbook/commands/WorkbookCommandsTest.cpp:140 (params->Set<TString>(DPI_SheetName, name1) -> ChangeWorkbookUIMode switches to that destination sheet); real UI producer modules/desktop/tabuischemaviewer/main/commands/SchemaViewerUICommands.cpp:926 sets it to switchToSheet
DPI_SheetName.how_to_obtain: Exact display name of the target sheet from the workbook (GetSheetsInfo or TWB). Same value space as DPI_Sheet; obtain the same way.
DPI_SheetName.gotchas: Goes through ValidateSheet -> when required, must match an existing sheet or BadValue. This is NOT the 'create a new sheet' name param -- a brand-new (not-yet-existing) sheet name uses DPI_NewSheet (wire 'new-sheet'), whose validation is INVERTED (BadValue if the sheet already exists). Unlike DPI_Sheet/Worksheet/Dashboard, DPI_SheetName is not marked 'implicit' (no automatic current-context fallback).

DPI_ShelfItemID.format: uint32_t (unsigned). A runtime id identifying a single shelf item / field pill within a viz. Serialized/consumed as a plain integer (params->Get<uint32_t>(DPI_ShelfItemID)). It is surfaced FROM the product in shelf-item pres models — codegen/doc/pres-models/calculation.data maps ShelfItem property ID -> DPI_ShelfItemID ('shelf item identifier for command parameters'). Used as an alternative selector: FieldCommands OneRequired<uint32_t, ConstSelectorCollectionPtr>(DPI_ShelfItemID, DPI_Selector), and ConstructSelectionParamFromID(viz, shelfItemId, ns) builds the runtime selection from it.
DPI_ShelfItemID.example: (runtime-assigned uint32_t; no stable literal — read from a shelf-item pres model)
DPI_ShelfItemID.how_to_obtain: It is a plain int on the wire, but the value is runtime-assigned and must be read first from a shelf/field pres model that exposes the ShelfItem 'ID' property (DPI_ShelfItemID), e.g. a shelf pres-model or the authoring shelf-item context menu builder. Once known, pass it as an integer to select that pill (a friendlier alternative to the non-serializable DPI_Selector).
DPI_ShelfItemID.gotchas: Not portable/stable across sessions or viz edits — it is per-viz runtime state. Where a command declares both shelf-item-id and selector, shelf-item-id is the agent-usable path (selector's serializer is a stub).

DPI_StoreId.format: Unsigned 32-bit integer (uint32_t on the wire - declared under the 'type: [ uint32_t, uint, simple ]' header, NOT a string). Same mechanism as controller-id: a ComponentID handle from the workbook's ComponentManager. Here the 'store' is a FilterStore (datasource/extract/quantitative filter store) registered as a component via componentManager.Add<FilterStore>(). Sequential from 1; 0 = invalid/no-store sentinel meaning worksheet-level filter.
DPI_StoreId.how_to_obtain: Runtime sequential integer handle valid only after invoking a Create*FilterStore command. Read the emitted store-id from the response: out StoreId param (filter-cmd.data:368 'Id of the filter cache created') or the returned ReleaseStoreCommand/ReleaseFilterStoreCmd carrying the id. Then pass that exact value back into editing/commit/release commands.
DPI_StoreId.gotchas: Same class as controller-id (per-session, ephemeral, reused, 0=invalid meaning no store / worksheet-level filter). Caller is contractually required to run the returned ReleaseStoreCommand/ReleaseFilterStoreCmd to free it. HasStoreId()/GetStoreId()!=0 is used to distinguish a datasource-filter flow from a worksheet filter.

DPI_Storyboard.format: The story's exact DISPLAY NAME as a plain string. Parameters::SetStoryboard -> Set<TString>(DPI_Storyboard, storyboard.Sheetname()); Parameters::GetStoryboard reads Get<TString>(DPI_Storyboard) and builds SheetLocator(name). (An optional stable SimpleIdentifier can accompany it via the separate key 'storyboarddoc-id'/DPI_StoryboardSimpleID, but the name string is the primary wire value.)
DPI_Storyboard.example_source: modules/integration_tests/current/tabdoc_integ/test/formalism/StoryboardDocTest.cpp:283 (parameters->Set<TString>(DPI_Dashboard, u"Story") for a story) and real UI producer modules/desktop/tabuilegacydashboard/main/storyboards/qtdesktop/StoryboardAuthoringPaneWidget.cpp:312 sets DPI_Storyboard to dashDoc->GetLocator()
DPI_Storyboard.how_to_obtain: Exact display name of the story/storyboard from the workbook (its title in the tab strip; TWB stores stories as sheets). Query via GetSheetsInfo / storyboard-names.
DPI_Storyboard.gotchas: ValidateParameters::ValidateStoryboard resolves and checks the name; a nonexistent name -> BadValue. Not a UUID. Empty/absent: HasStoryboard falls back to the current storyboard context ('implicit'). The DecoratedHex UUID form belongs to DPI_StoryboardSimpleID (key 'storyboarddoc-id'), not to this 'storyboard' key.

DPI_TableName.format: A QualifiedName serialized to its bracketed-dotted string form. Declared type [QualifiedName, string, simple] wired to serializers/CoreParameterTypeSerializers.h (codegen/data/params.data:498-509). Serializer QualifiedNameSerializer: TypeToString -> QualifiedName::GetFullValue(); TypeFromString -> QualifiedName::ParseGlobal(str). Wire form is components each wrapped in [ ] and joined by '.': single component => "[Table]"; two components => "[Schema].[Table]". A literal closing bracket ']' inside a component is escaped by doubling it ']]'. Leading/trailing whitespace is trimmed on parse; empty string is the valid empty QualifiedName.
DPI_TableName.example_source: modules/integration_tests/current/tabdocobjectgraph_integ/test/ObjectModelCommandIntegTest.cpp:3453 (params->Set<QualifiedName>(DPI_TableName, QualifiedName(X_TABLE)) with X_TABLE=u"X$" -> GetFullValue "[X$]"); two-component form documented in modules/platform/tabcoredata/public/data/QualifiedName.h:52 ("[CoffeeChain_MDB].[Product]"); wrapper default QualifiedName() in codegen/doc/command-wrappers/dataconnection-cmd.data:61
DPI_TableName.how_to_obtain: Construct the bracketed string from the real table name reported by the connection: single unqualified table => "[Orders]"; schema-qualified => "[dbo].[Orders]". Escape any ']' as ']]'. The actual name components must match what the connection/data source exposes (query connection metadata or the object-graph node's TableName field, wire key table-name, present on connection/data-source pres-models). The string FORMAT is agent-constructable, but the specific components must correspond to an existing table.
DPI_TableName.gotchas: Wire value is the bracketed form ("[Table]"), NOT the bare table name ("Table") and NOT a UUID. Do not JSON-nest components; it is a single flat string. Malformed input (missing '[' , unbalanced brackets, dangling '.') throws QualifiedNameException at parse time. Note codegen has two params.data files: DPI_TableName lives in codegen/data/params.data (NOT codegen/doc/params.data).

DPI_TableNames.format: A JSON array whose elements are each a QualifiedName in the bracketed-dotted string form (see DPI_TableName). Declared type [QualifiedName, string, simplearray, , QualifiedName] wired to serializers/CoreParameterTypeSerializers.h (codegen/data/params.data:512-522). Held in C++ as std::vector<QualifiedName>. On the External Client / Agent JSON wire the value is a list category (PTC_List): JSONSpiritParse parses val.get_array(), serializes each element to a string, and passes them to the serializer's FromStringList. So the wire value is a JSON array of QualifiedName strings, e.g. ["[Orders]", "[dbo].[Products]"].
DPI_TableNames.example_source: codegen/ui/command-wrappers/objectmodel-ui-cmd.data:11 ([in, tableNames,, DPI_TableNames, required,, "Vector of QualifiedName to be added as objects"]); C++ get/set as vector<QualifiedName>: modules/desktop/tabui/main/connection/commands/ConnectionUICommands.cpp:3082 (params->Set<vector<QualifiedName>>(DPI_TableNames, tableNames)), :3112, TableDragConverter.cpp:31; array parse path modules/platform/tabpreslayer/main/serializers/JSONSpiritParse.cpp:115-133,238-273
DPI_TableNames.how_to_obtain: Build a JSON array of bracketed QualifiedName strings, one per table (same construction rules as DPI_TableName). Component names must match tables the connection exposes; obtain candidate names from connection/schema metadata queries. Order is preserved as a list.
DPI_TableNames.gotchas: Each element must be the bracketed form ("[Table]"), not a bare name. It is a real JSON array (PTC_List) — do not pass a single delimited string. Elements are parsed individually via ParseGlobal, so a malformed element throws QualifiedNameException. Like DPI_TableName, defined in codegen/data/params.data (line 522), not codegen/doc/params.data.

DPI_TargetPt.format: PointPresModel struct (JSON object) with two integer fields: x (DPI_X) and y (DPI_Y), both default 0. Maps 1:1 to a Qt QPoint. Coordinate space: viewport/scene-relative integer PIXELS, origin top-left, y increasing downward (device-independent screen pixels, NOT data coordinates, NOT fractional). Used as the location an annotation points to (the user's right-click position in the visible viz scene).
DPI_TargetPt.example_source: modules/platform/tabdoc/test/presentation-model/SimpleTypesHelpersTest.cpp:74-86 (x=11,y=23 round-trip QPointFromPointPresModel); mark annotations use dummy {x:0,y:0} (tableau.extensions.1.latest.js:8622)
DPI_TargetPt.how_to_obtain: Mark annotations (AE_Mark): trivially yes - pass {x:0,y:0}; the target is derived from the current mark selection, not the point (SDK sends a dummy). Point/Area annotations (AE_Point/AE_Area): must be a real viewport-pixel location inside the pane where the annotation should point; only reliable if you know the current render geometry/scroll state (comes from an actual click position). CreateAnnotationCommand adds GetScrollOffsetOfContentOfScene() to convert viewport-relative to scene-content pixels.
DPI_TargetPt.gotchas: The incoming point is viewport-relative; the command adds the current scroll offset before use, so supplying absolute content coordinates offsets the annotation by the scroll amount. Origin top-left. Values are integers; readback path truncates fractional coords via static_cast<int>. AE_Area treats the point as pixels and builds a +/-50px rect around it.

DPI_VisualID.format: C++ VisualID struct = { SheetLocator worksheet, SheetLocator dashboard, WindowLocator }. Its wire serializer (VisualIDSerializer) emits an object with only two string properties: worksheet (DPI_Worksheet) and dashboard (DPI_Dashboard). DEPRECATED: the serializer header carries a REMOVE note ('VisualIDSerializer is deprecated ... now we use DPI_VisualIDPM, which corresponds to VisualIDPresModelSerializer'). In params.data the param is flagged 'implicit', meaning the framework sets it from live context, not the caller. There is no plain scalar 'visual id' string; a viz is identified by its worksheet name (plus optional dashboard name).
DPI_VisualID.example_source: VisualSerializers.cpp VisualIDSerializer::ToSerializer (emits DPI_Worksheet + DPI_Dashboard); shape only, deprecated path — no live wire capture found
DPI_VisualID.how_to_obtain: Not agent-facing. Deprecated in favor of DPI_VisualIDPM. The underlying identity is the worksheet name (and, for embedded viz, the dashboard name); use sheet-name navigation (navigate-to-sheet) instead of trying to pass a visual-id.
DPI_VisualID.gotchas: Marked DEPRECATED in source and 'implicit' in params.data. Not a string/int — a struct. Do not confuse with window-id (a UUID). The live/preferred representation is DPI_VisualIDPM, not this.

DPI_VisualIDPM.format: C++ ConstVisualIDPresModelPtr -> generated VisualIDPresModel pres-model. Serialized as a JSON object whose properties come from codegen/doc/pres-models/visual-id.data: worksheet (DPI_Worksheet, string, required), dashboard (DPI_Dashboard, string, optional — omitted when empty), storyboard (DPI_Storyboard, string, optional — omitted when empty), flipboard-zone-id (DPI_FlipboardZoneID, DEPRECATED, omitted when 0), story-point-id (DPI_StoryPointID, int, optional — omitted when 0). It is the non-deprecated replacement for DPI_VisualID. Flagged 'implicit' in params.data.
DPI_VisualIDPM.example_source: codegen/doc/pres-models/visual-id.data (property/wire-key mapping); values illustrative — pres-model is built at runtime by BuildVisualIDPresModel
DPI_VisualIDPM.how_to_obtain: Structurally it is just names, so an object like {"worksheet":"<sheet name>"} is composable. BUT it is populated at runtime by BuildVisualIDPresModel(IWorkbookAccessor, VisualID), which validates the sheet exists in the workbook (throws LogicException if not) and resolves story path (storyboard/story-point-id). Real values are surfaced in pres models such as GetSheetsInfo/workbook (DPI_VisualIDPMs 'visual-ids' collection) and explain-data-pane. Prefer reading it from a pres-model query rather than hand-building.
DPI_VisualIDPM.gotchas: This is exactly the type the goto-sheet doc calls runtime-only: CONFIRMED — it is flagged 'implicit' (framework sets it from the active/selected viz) and building it requires a live IWorkbookAccessor that validates the sheet and resolves the story path, so a hand-built value can fail validation. A plain 'visual-id' string is NOT obtainable; the identifying data is the worksheet name plus optional dashboard/storyboard/story-point-id.

DPI_WindowID.format: DPI_WindowID is a SimpleIdentifier serialized as a string via SimpleIdentifierSerializer -> SimpleIdentifier::ToString() -> TUUID DecoratedHex. Canonical form (Qt QUuid::toString default, uppercased in Tableau): {XXXXXXXX-XXXX-XXXX-XXXX-XXXXXXXXXXXX}. Braces are optional on parse but product wire examples include them. It is NOT a C++ WindowLocator object on the wire -- only the UUID string.
DPI_WindowID.how_to_obtain: Read a real window-id from TWB/TWBX <windows>/<window>/<simple-id uuid='{...}'/> (stable for saved windows only), or from GetSheetsInfo -> each SheetInfo.window-id. No dedicated 'list window ids' agent query is surfaced in the curated catalog. PREFER navigate-to-sheet + { "sheet": "<exact name>" } for flip-by-name; do not hand-invent a UUID.
DPI_WindowID.gotchas: Passing a sheet display name or an invented/stale UUID as window-id -> BadValue, which surfaces as an opaque Agent HTTP 500. Empty/omitted window-id with an active sheet -> silent no-op (Parameters::GetWindow falls back to GetCurrentWindow(); returns ok:true with no flip). New unsaved sheets get runtime UUIDs not yet on disk. goto-sheet also accepts an undeclared 'sheet' fallback (DPI_Sheet) at runtime, but catalogs may reject it -- prefer navigate-to-sheet.

DPI_Worksheet.format: The worksheet's exact DISPLAY NAME as a plain string (a SheetLocator built from the name via SheetLocator(name); NOT a UUID, path, or object). Parameters::SetVisualId/SetWorksheet serialize it as Set<TString>(DPI_Worksheet, locator.Sheetname()). Only for a story-point (ephemeral) worksheet is a SheetPath object emitted instead, under the sibling key 'worksheet-pm' (DPI_WorksheetPM); persistent worksheets always use the plain name string.
DPI_Worksheet.example_source: modules/platform/tabdoc/test/serializers/UberTipSerializersTest.cpp:125 (params2->Set<TString>(DPI_Worksheet, u"name")); real UI producer modules/desktop/tabui/main/summarycard/commands/SummaryCardUICommands.cpp:39 sets it to the live worksheetName
DPI_Worksheet.how_to_obtain: Use the exact worksheet display name from the workbook. Query it via GetSheetsInfo (each SheetInfo has the sheet name), or read <worksheet name='...'> from the TWB. Name must be the on-screen title, case/whitespace exact.
DPI_Worksheet.gotchas: ValidateParameters::ValidateWorksheet resolves the name to a SheetLocator and calls workbook HasSheet; a name that does not match an existing worksheet -> BadValue. Do NOT pass a dashboard name here (DPI_Worksheet is WorksheetDoc-only; dashboards use DPI_Dashboard). A UUID or braced-UUID string is wrong for this key (that is DPI_WindowID). Empty string when required -> BadValue; when optional/absent it falls back to the current worksheet context (params.data marks it 'implicit').

DPI_ZoneID.format: Unsigned 32-bit integer (uint32_t), 1-based per-dashboard zone id. Declared in params.data under the type block `[ uint32_t, uint, simple, * ]`. In the legacy command string it appears quoted (zone-id="2") but the value is a plain integer; on the JSON/Agent wire it is a JSON number. Value 0 means the dashboard root (ParentZoneID 0 = root) and is also reused as a null/clear-selection sentinel (NullIdToClearSelection).
DPI_ZoneID.example_source: modules/integration_tests/current/tabdoc_integ/test/formalism/StoryboardDocTest.cpp:282 (`parameters->Set<uint32_t>(DPI_ZoneID, 3 /*hard coded zone id for the title zone*/)`); legacy string form `zone-id="2"` in modules/integration_tests/current/tabdocdashboard_integ/main/objects/ToggleButtonTests.cpp:1313
DPI_ZoneID.how_to_obtain: It is a plain integer, but the specific value is a live-session runtime id you must query. Run `tabdoc:get-dashboard` (in-param `dashboard` = dashboard name) → DashboardPresModel, whose ZoneCommon list items each expose `ZoneID` (DPI_ZoneID, described in codegen as 'The uint32_t 1-based zone ID'). Many mutating commands also echo DPI_ZoneID back in their command result (e.g. add-zone returns the new zone id).
DPI_ZoneID.gotchas: 1-based and per-dashboard; assigned by the running session in creation order, not a stable persisted UUID. 0 == dashboard root AND is the clear-selection sentinel, so never treat 0 as a real target. Marked `implicit` in params.data. DPI_ZoneID is currently the required singular param while DPI_ZoneIDs is the optional plural (see DashboardCommandsCreateParams.cpp).

DPI_ZoneIDs.format: List of uint32_t zone ids. Declared under params.data type block `[ uint32_t, uint, simplearray, *, uint32_t ]`; C++ type is `std::vector<uint32_t>`. Legacy command-string serialization is a bracketed comma list: `zone-ids=[3]` / `zone-ids=[3,5,7]`. On the JSON/Agent wire it is a JSON array of integers. Each element is a DPI_ZoneID-style 1-based zone id.

DPI_ZoneIDs.how_to_obtain: Same source as DPI_ZoneID: query `tabdoc:get-dashboard` -> DashboardPresModel ZoneCommon list -> collect ZoneID values into the array. Values are live runtime ids, not agent-inventable.
DPI_ZoneIDs.gotchas: Transitional param: `DPI_ZoneID` is currently required and `DPI_ZoneIDs` optional; internal code copies the first element of ZoneIDs into the singular ZoneID (DashboardCommandsCreateParams.cpp:23-28 `AddSingleZoneIDForRequiredParam`). May be returned empty (CopyZoneTests.cpp:440).
